targets: Different NHTSA component domain than brakes (AIR BAGS). Sanity check that retrieval isn't just always returning the brake cluster it was tuned on.
incident_text: THE CONTACT OWNS A 2019 HONDA CR-V. THE CONTACT STATED THAT WHILE TRAVELING APPROXIMATELY 35 MPH, ANOTHER VEHICLE STRUCK THE FRONT OF THE VEHICLE IN A HEAD-ON COLLISION. THE FRONTAL AIRBAGS FAILED TO DEPLOY DURING THE CRASH. THE VEHICLE SUSTAINED SIGNIFICANT FRONT-END DAMAGE AND THE CONTACT AND PASSENGER SUFFERED CHEST AND FACIAL INJURIES THAT THE CONTACT BELIEVED WOULD HAVE BEEN MITIGATED HAD THE AIRBAGS DEPLOYED. THE VEHICLE WAS TOWED TO A DEALER FOR INSPECTION. THE DEALER STATED THE AIRBAG CONTROL MODULE DID NOT REGISTER A DEPLOYMENT EVENT. THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 41,200.

targets: Deliberately ambiguous causation (throttle body vs. floor mat entrapment vs. software) to stress-test the fix for bug #2 -- evaluation_node must accept 2-3 well-cited plausible causes instead of forcing a single root cause or looping forever.
incident_text: THE CONTACT OWNS A 2021 TOYOTA CAMRY. THE CONTACT STATED THAT WHILE DECELERATING TO A STOP AT AN INTERSECTION, THE VEHICLE SUDDENLY ACCELERATED WITHOUT WARNING. THE CONTACT APPLIED THE BRAKE PEDAL BUT THE VEHICLE CONTINUED TO ACCELERATE UNTIL IT STRUCK A UTILITY POLE. THE CONTACT STATED THE FLOOR MAT WAS PROPERLY SECURED AND DID NOT INTERFERE WITH THE PEDALS. THE VEHICLE WAS TOWED TO A DEALER. THE DEALER WAS UNABLE TO DUPLICATE THE FAILURE AND FOUND NO STORED DIAGNOSTIC TROUBLE CODES RELATED TO THE THROTTLE BODY. THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 18,900.

targets: Safety-critical mechanical failure that usually DOES have a single dominant cause in the literature (power steering assist failure). Contrast case for EVAL-02: if evaluation_node lets this one slide with a vague multi-cause hedge too, the fix for bug #2 has been overcorrected into rubber-stamping everything.
incident_text: THE CONTACT OWNS A 2018 FORD ESCAPE. THE CONTACT STATED THAT WHILE TRAVELING APPROXIMATELY 60 MPH ON A HIGHWAY, THE ELECTRIC POWER STEERING ASSIST SUDDENLY FAILED AND THE STEERING WHEEL BECAME EXTREMELY DIFFICULT TO TURN. THE CONTACT WAS ABLE TO MANEUVER THE VEHICLE TO THE SHOULDER WITHOUT A CRASH. A WARNING LIGHT FOR THE POWER STEERING SYSTEM ILLUMINATED ON THE INSTRUMENT PANEL AT THE TIME OF THE FAILURE. THE VEHICLE WAS TAKEN TO AN INDEPENDENT MECHANIC WHO DIAGNOSED A FAILED ELECTRIC POWER STEERING ASSIST MOTOR. THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 52,300.

targets: Picked because EV battery/charging fire complaints tend to cluster densely and look alike near-duplicates (same phrasing: 'smoke', 'fire', 'while charging'). This re-stresses bug #1 (HNSW recall collapse) on a NEW cluster, not the brake cluster you already fixed against.
incident_text: THE CONTACT OWNS A 2022 CHEVROLET BOLT EV. THE CONTACT STATED THAT WHILE THE VEHICLE WAS PARKED AND CHARGING OVERNIGHT IN THE GARAGE, THE HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY PACK BEGAN EMITTING SMOKE FOLLOWED BY FLAMES. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS CALLED AND EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE, BUT THE VEHICLE AND PART OF THE GARAGE WERE DESTROYED. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. THE MANUFACTURER'S FIELD REPRESENTATIVE INSPECTED THE REMAINS AND ATTRIBUTED THE FIRE TO A DEFECT IN THE BATTERY CELL MANUFACTURING PROCESS. THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 9,400.

targets: Shares surface vocabulary with EVAL-04 (fire, smoke, smell) but is a completely different causal mechanism (mechanical fuel leak, not electrical/battery). Designed to re-trigger bug #3 -- semantic similarity != causal similarity -- if retrieval or the analysis_node cross-cites an EV battery-fire case as 'supporting evidence' for a fuel-system fire.
incident_text: THE CONTACT OWNS A 2017 JEEP GRAND CHEROKEE. THE CONTACT STATED THAT WHILE DRIVING AT APPROXIMATELY 45 MPH, THE CONTACT NOTICED A STRONG SMELL OF GASOLINE ENTERING THE CABIN FOLLOWED BY SMOKE COMING FROM UNDER THE HOOD. THE CONTACT SAFELY PULLED OVER AND EXITED THE VEHICLE BEFORE FLAMES BECAME VISIBLE NEAR THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT. THE VEHICLE WAS A TOTAL LOSS. THE CONTACT STATED A FUEL RAIL CONNECTOR HAD CRACKED, ALLOWING FUEL TO LEAK ONTO THE HOT ENGINE BLOCK. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE ISSUE. THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 76,500.
